cases.description: One eligible checkout creates one reservation and one captured payment.
cases.expected: One ledger transaction and at most one Purchase per approved platform route with exact USD cents.

cases.description: One checkout creates two tee-time reservations.
cases.expected: One transaction value is counted once unless Tock supplies an authoritative allocation rule.

cases.description: The identical webhook event is delivered more than once under Tock's at-least-once contract.
cases.expected: One processed event, one ledger effect, and zero duplicate purchases.

cases.description: A stale reservation update arrives after a newer sequence.
cases.expected: The stale state is ignored or quarantined without reversing the newer state.

cases.description: A browser Purchase and server Purchase represent the same checkout.
cases.expected: Meta receives the same event name and event ID and records one deduplicated purchase.

cases.description: A paid checkout receives a partial refund.
cases.expected: Ledger net value changes by exact cents; platform adjustment follows only a verified supported path.

cases.description: A paid checkout receives a full refund.
cases.expected: Ledger net value becomes zero; Google retraction or restatement is tested when configured.

cases.description: A prepaid reservation is cancelled and no refund is issued.
cases.expected: Cancellation state changes while captured revenue remains according to the approved definition.

cases.description: A reservation is cancelled and replaced by another booking.
cases.expected: The original and replacement remain traceable without double-counting value.

cases.description: A prepaid reservation is marked no-show without a refund.
cases.expected: Operational status changes while prepaid value remains; no-show is not treated as an automatic refund.

cases.description: A reservation is transferred to another guest.
cases.expected: The original reservation is recorded as cancelled and the transferee receives a new reservation; value is linked without an unsupported second purchase.

cases.description: The same business, reservation ID, and versionId arrive with a different payload hash.
cases.expected: The update is quarantined as a conflict and does not replace the accepted state.

cases.description: The business-group webhook sends valid reservations for Puttery locations other than NYC.
cases.expected: Non-NYC records receive a successful filtered acknowledgment and never enter the NYC ledger or ad delivery.

cases.description: A webhook delivery is missed after Tock's immediate retry attempts.
cases.expected: The next daily export reconciliation restores the missing reservation version without creating a duplicate.

cases.description: An event arrives for another Puttery business or location.
cases.expected: The event receives a successful filtered acknowledgment, does not retain its source identifiers, and never enters NYC reporting or ad delivery.

cases.description: A booking has no permitted advertising-measurement consent.
cases.expected: The ledger may retain non-identifying aggregate facts, but no guest match signals are sent to ad platforms.

cases.description: A valid paid booking contains no usable click or browser identifiers.
cases.expected: The booking remains visible as unmatched and is not represented as a failed or guaranteed platform match.

cases.description: A server event falls outside Meta's accepted event-time window.
cases.expected: The event is withheld or quarantined so one stale record cannot invalidate a production batch.
